key_insight: FAMOSE uses the ReAct (reasoning + acting) paradigm to autonomously generate, evaluate, and refine candidate features for tabular data, combining generation and selection in a closed-loop to find high-impact feature augmentations without heavy domain expertise.
problem_solved: Automates the hard, combinatorial task of feature engineering for tabular ML—reducing manual effort and expertise needed to discover useful feature transformations from an exponentially large search space.
method: A ReAct agent alternates between reasoning (proposing feature transformations and combinations) and acting (applying/generating candidate features) in an iterative loop.
Model-in-the-loop evaluation scores and ranks candidates; selection and pruning are integrated to keep the search tractable (e.g., heuristics, beam search, regularization).
Refinement cycles incorporate feedback (performance, sparsity, interpretability) so the agent converges on a compact, high-value feature set.
impact: FAMOSE streamlines and democratizes feature engineering for tabular problems—speeding development, improving predictive performance, and reducing dependence on domain experts while maintaining interpretable feature sets.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram showing ReAct loop: propose → generate → evaluate → select → refine
Before/after tabular example: original features vs. discovered augmentations with resulting model metrics (accuracy/AUC/Δ)
Search visualization: beam/search tree pruned over iterations to illustrate candidate exploration and convergence
Bar/line chart comparing performance and feature count against baselines (manual features, standard AutoML)
paper_title: FAMOSE: A ReAct Approach to Automated Feature Discovery
paper_authors: Keith Burghardt, Jienan Liu, Sadman Sakib, Yuning Hao, Bo Li
